# PDFAD — PDF Agent Descriptor

> Self-describing manifest embedded in a PDF — element index, design DNA, edit journal, engine capabilities — so AI agents understand the document without re-parsing it.

PDFAD defines a self-describing manifest embedded inside a PDF (embedded file agent_manifest.json or XMP pdfad:manifest). A pdfadged document explains itself to agents: its element index, its Design DNA, its edit journal, and what an engine is allowed to do.

Version 1.0 (Working Draft), Apache-2.0. Author: fjjjuv. Reference implementation: pdfbadger (https://github.com/fjjjuv/pdfbadger).

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://fjjjuv.github.io/pdfad/): what it is and why
- [Specification](https://fjjjuv.github.io/pdfad/spec.html): full normative spec v1.0 (rendered)
- [Specification source](https://github.com/fjjjuv/pdfad/blob/main/SPEC.md): raw markdown
- [Examples](https://fjjjuv.github.io/pdfad/examples.html): worked example documents
- [Full spec for LLMs](https://fjjjuv.github.io/pdfad/llms-full.txt): complete spec text

## Related specifications

- [PDFSP — PDF Scene Patch](https://github.com/fjjjuv/pdfsp): elements_index.id_scheme defines the ids PDFSP selectors use
- [PDFDTP — Document Transaction Protocol](https://github.com/fjjjuv/pdfdtp): journal_head and capabilities reflect DTP journal/certificate state
